memo.summary: Merstham Software sells booking software to UK trades with very sticky retention; the base grows itself.
memo.what_it_does: Booking and job-management software for UK trades — plumbers, electricians, small contractors.
memo.how_it_earns: Per-seat monthly subscriptions plus a take rate on payments; net revenue retention above 115%.
bear: SMB churn rises in a downturn.
A large platform could bundle a rival product.
Price is already at the top of its range.
memo.bear_hardest: If NRR falls below 105% the compounding story is over, and the multiple is not priced for that.
gaps: Churn is disclosed only as an annual NRR figure.
Payment take-rate is not broken out.

tv.summary: Merstham Software sells booking software to UK trades — plumbers, electricians, small contractors — with very sticky retention.
tv.variant_view: Growth looks ordinary, but net revenue retention above 115% means the existing base grows itself; the market still prices it as a low-growth SMB vendor.
tv.assumptions: ["net revenue retention stays above 110%","no major platform competitor enters"]
tv.risks: SMB churn in a downturn; a big platform could bundle a rival.
tv.invalidation: NRR falls below 105% for two reporting periods.
tv.exit_conditions: Thesis invalidated, or the position reaches its target weight through price alone.
tv.reason_for_change: Tightened the invalidation condition after the interim update.
